title: References: Resolving Between Resources
description: FHIR is normalized: a MedicationRequest doesn't embed the drug — it points at a Medication resource by reference string. Learn the reference anatomy (type prefix + logical id), extract ids with string functions, follow references to their target with resolve(), and detect dangling references that point at nothing.
learningObjectives: Read the raw reference string from a Reference element via the choice-type cast
Extract the logical id from 'Type/id' with Split and Last
Check a reference's type prefix with StartsWith
Follow a reference to its target resource with resolve()
Filter and match on the resolved resource's coding (RxNorm)
Detect dangling references — resolve() of a missing target is null

hints.message: (R.medication as FHIR.Reference).reference — medication is a choice type; cast it to Reference, then take .reference for the string.
Last(Split((R.medication as FHIR.Reference).reference, '/')) — split on the slash and take the final segment: the logical id.
StartsWith((R.medication as FHIR.Reference).reference, 'Medication/') — the type prefix comes before the slash.
resolve((R.medication as FHIR.Reference)) returns the referenced resource itself (found in the resources table by type + id) — or null if it doesn't exist.

exists([MedicationRequest] R where R.status = 'active' and exists(resolve(R.medication as FHIR.Reference).code.coding C where C.code = '5640' and C.system = 'http://www.nlm.nih.gov/research/umls/rxnorm')) — navigate the resolved resource like any other.
resolve() of a missing target is null — "Active Request Count" > 0 and "Resolved Med Code" is null flags a request whose medication can't be resolved.
